note: The release gate's allowlist: a gating checker (run-checks.py CHECKS minus REPORT_ONLY) may fail at a release only when this file names every finding line it prints. run-checks.py applies it itself (tools/gate_allowlist.py), so a bare `python tools/run-checks.py` and refresh-safe.sh give the same verdict, and a pass over an allowlisted failure says `PASS with N allowlisted failure(s)`, never a bare PASS. Since r14 (3 November 2026, CHG-R14I-001; the r13 system review E-01, E-02, E-04): an entry carries `added`, `expires` (at most 14 days after `added`, CLAUDE.md rule 15), `approved_by` (the lead), `change` (the CHG-/CR- id) and `why`; each `known` pattern (Python regex, re.search) names ONE finding, never a count or a verdict line; a checker that crashed is never let through. An undated, unapproved, expired or count-pinned entry fails the gate itself (run-checks.py, and check-baseline-ratchet.py on every run). Emptied at r14: the three checkers listed until r13 (check-authored-inputs, check-screen-patterns, check-screen-permissions) had undated entries 14 to 33 days old; they are fixed, or what is left is with the lead.

<checker name>.why: what fails and why it may ship once

refresh_tools_coverage.why: refresh.sh ends by failing when tools/ holds a .py it neither runs nor names in _EXCLUDED; refresh-safe.sh runs the block and fails on a name not allowlisted here (entries as above). Empty since 1 October: every tool is run or excused in _EXCLUDED.
